fyPerformance: Q2 consolidated operating revenue grew 22% to ₹2,484 Cr, operating EBITDA rose 24% to ₹706 Cr at 28.4% margin (+50 bps), and PAT increased 23% to ₹349 Cr.
Consolidated hotel segment revenue and EBITDA grew 25% and 30%; standalone operating revenue was ₹1,336 Cr (+26%) and operating EBITDA ₹520 Cr (+40%), with margin up 400 bps to 38.9%.

Standalone RevPAR grew 28% and consolidated domestic hotel RevPAR 25%; occupancy rose to 82% from 75% a year earlier. Taj Palace Delhi room revenue increased 132% and monthly revenue topped ₹100 Cr in September.
H1 saw 47 hotels signed and 20 opened; the portfolio reached 670 hotels with over 69,000 keys in operation or development, including 390 operating hotels. Gross cash reserves exceeded ₹4,350 Cr.

highlights: The company said it delivered its 18th consecutive record quarter despite West Asia-related airline and travel disruption; growth was supported by domestic demand and MICE.
Ginger revenue reached ₹193 Cr (+25%) at 40% EBITDA margin; Ginger had 100 operating hotels and was on track for 150 by March 2027.
Management fee income grew 25% to ₹156 Cr, supported by managed room inventory (+25%), RevPAR, technical fees and new brand fees.
The proposed Oriental Hotels merger is expected to take effect no earlier than 1 April 2027; management estimated a 6%–7% uplift to standalone operating revenue in FY28, separate from FY27 guidance.
Indian Hotels Company Ltd.whatChanged: IHCL raised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance from 12–14% to 15–17% and added a 17–19% hotel segment range; Q2 consolidated revenue grew 22%, with hotel segment revenue up 25%.
risks: TajSATS airline catering faced flight-capacity cuts and geopolitical disruption; management called FY27 a consolidation year and said non-aviation catering is lower margin.

International businesses remained exposed to West Asia travel disruption and higher fuel/power costs; London also faced the end of a property-tax waiver, while management said H2 trends were improving.
The 50-hotel FY27 opening plan still requires 30 openings in H2; Oriental Hotels merger benefits are excluded from FY27 and depend on completion in FY28.

sectorSummary.overview: The seven available calls show higher room rates and revenue, supported by domestic business, events and leisure demand. IHCL raised annual growth guidance and Leela expects a stronger full year, but project timing, tax effects, travel disruption and funding requirements make individual results uneven. Apeejay and EIH await calls.

trends.text: Higher room rates and RevPAR supported revenue growth, with occupancy trends varying by portfolio and market.
Operators are adding or repositioning rooms and expanding portfolios; construction, approvals and hotel stabilization shape the timing of earnings.

tailwinds.text: Domestic business travel, MICE and social events support room and food-and-beverage demand across major hotel markets.
Pricing, asset upgrades and operating efficiency provide scope for stronger earnings as demand and new properties mature.

opportunities.text: Managed hotels, franchise fees and other fee-led platforms offer growth alongside owned or leased inventory.
New hotels and repositioned properties can broaden market exposure, but forecast contributions depend on opening and ramp-up.

risks.text: Large development programs and approvals can delay room additions and cash generation; Delhi construction restrictions are an explicit Chalet risk.
Foreign travel disruption, flight capacity and energy costs affect markets differently; stronger domestic demand does not eliminate these exposures.
Growth investment requires balance-sheet discipline; debt ratios, refinancing and development capital should be assessed on each company’s stated basis.

insights.text: Guidance is selective: IHCL raised FY27 revenue growth to 15–17%; Leela expects a better full year but its high-teens EBITDA outlook specifically concerns H2.
Profit comparisons require adjustments: Chalet reports a deferred-tax credit, SAMHI separates GST effects and prior exceptional gains, and Lemon Tree distinguishes net EBITDA from hotel EBITDAR.
